companyDescription: Enterprise conversational/voice AI · Casey's, OpenTable partnerships · 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for Conversational AI · real $300M ATM dilution overhang
priceNote: Self-fetched today (no live-prices.json cache yet). Down 1.91% today, down ~71% from the 52-week high ($22.17) after a $300M at-the-market offering announcement and legal-scrutiny headlines both weighed on the stock this year.
summary: This refresh needs to be honest: SoundHound's real upside has compressed well below the typical turbo bar. The 7-analyst consensus is $13.14 (+104% from here) — real and broad, but not close to 200%. The underlying business has genuine momentum (Casey's AI-ordering deployment expanded to 2,600+ locations handling 21M+ guest interactions, a 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader ranking, a new 'Sales Assist' AI agent), but the stock fell to under $7 specifically because management launched a $300M at-the-market offering to fund ongoing losses and M&A — a real, disclosed dilution overhang, not analyst speculation. ⚠️ SURVIVAL: this isn't a going-concern situation (2026 revenue is guided $225-260M), but the active $300M ATM is exactly the kind of overhang this skill's survival check exists to flag. Included here as an honest carryover update, not a fresh high-conviction pick — real story, compressed math.

catalysts.name: Casey's Partnership Expansion

catalysts.name: $300M ATM Offering
catalysts.description: A $300M at-the-market equity program (plus a broad shelf registration) launched in early May 2026 to fund OASYS development and M&A — real dilution risk if fully tapped, and the direct cause of a Jul selloff.

risks: ⚠️ SURVIVAL: the $300M ATM is a real, active dilution mechanism launched specifically to fund ongoing losses and M&A — every share issued under it dilutes existing holders, and the company has already tapped equity markets aggressively this cycle
Real upside (7-analyst consensus +104%) no longer clears the ~200% floor this board typically screens for — this is now a compressed, borderline pick, not a clean moonshot
Legal scrutiny headlines (referenced in recent coverage) add a real, if unquantified, tail risk on top of the dilution overhang
Revenue growth is decelerating and Q1 gross margin fell to 31% — real fundamental softening, not just a sentiment problem
Down ~71% from the 52-week high — a large re-rate has already happened; the easy multiple-compression move may be mostly behind rather than ahead

macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM-HIGH — the $300M ATM makes this name unusually sensitive to the rate/financing environment right now; a hawkish Jul 28-29 FOMC surprise would make every dollar raised under that program more dilutive.
